problems.description: Employees receive spear-phishing emails impersonating executives requesting urgent wire transfers or sensitive data, exploiting trust and urgency to bypass normal verification.
risk_reduction: Implement email authentication protocols like DMARC, DKIM, and SPF
Conduct targeted phishing awareness training focusing on social engineering tactics
Establish verification procedures for financial or sensitive requests via alternate communication channels

problems.description: Phishing emails contain malicious attachments disguised as invoices or reports that, when opened, deploy malware to compromise endpoints.
risk_reduction: Deploy advanced email filtering and sandboxing to detect malicious attachments
Restrict execution of macros and scripts in email attachments
Educate users on verifying unexpected attachments before opening

problems.description: Credential harvesting sites mimic corporate login portals, tricking employees into submitting usernames and passwords, leading to account compromise.
risk_reduction: Use multi-factor authentication (MFA) to reduce impact of stolen credentials
Implement browser and network-level anti-phishing tools
Regularly update and communicate official URLs and login procedures

problems.description: Attackers send phishing emails targeting cloud administrators with links to fake cloud console login pages to steal credentials and gain unauthorized access.
risk_reduction: Enforce MFA on all cloud accounts
Use conditional access policies to restrict login locations and devices
Train cloud admins to recognize phishing attempts and verify URLs carefully

problems.description: Phishing campaigns deliver links to malicious cloud-hosted documents that exploit browser vulnerabilities to install malware or steal session tokens.
risk_reduction: Implement web filtering to block access to known malicious URLs
Keep browsers and plugins up to date with security patches
Educate users on risks of clicking unknown links and opening unexpected documents

problems.description: Compromised cloud email accounts are used to send phishing emails internally, increasing trust and likelihood of successful attacks.
risk_reduction: Monitor email sending patterns for anomalies
Use anomaly detection to flag unusual login locations or devices
Promptly investigate and remediate compromised accounts

problems.description: Individuals receive SMS or messaging app phishing (smishing) messages impersonating banks or services, tricking them into revealing personal or financial information.
risk_reduction: Advise users to verify sender authenticity and avoid clicking links in unsolicited messages
Use mobile security apps with phishing detection capabilities
Encourage enabling MFA on personal accounts

problems.description: Phishing emails target personal users with fake notifications about account suspensions or prize winnings, prompting them to enter credentials on fraudulent websites.
risk_reduction: Educate users on recognizing common phishing tactics and verifying communications
Use email providers with strong spam and phishing filters
Promote use of password managers to detect fake login pages

problems.description: Social media phishing involves attackers sending direct messages with malicious links or fake friend requests to harvest credentials or spread malware.
risk_reduction: Enable privacy settings to limit messages from unknown users
Be cautious about clicking links or downloading files from social media
Report and block suspicious accounts promptly
